claims.text: A native app is written for one platform (Android, iOS) in its own language and tools; cross-platform is one code base built for several platforms, as Flutter does for web, Android, iOS. An HTML web framework makes pages from HTML elements; Flutter web draws the screen itself.
claims.source_hint: content/glossary.yaml native-app, cross-platform; Flutter docs: supported platforms; web FAQ / renderers

claims.text: A Flutter project is built for a platform once it has that platform's folder, which flutter create --platforms adds. In DonHang.App, android/ or ios/ lets the same Dart code be built there; it works there once the two browser_web.dart files also get a version for it.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: flutter create --platforms / adding a platform to an existing project

claims.text: ADR 0017 (Accepted) context: customers order mostly from phone browsers; a few shops asked for an installed app; some shops want product pages found via search engines; all three are assumptions from talks with shops, not measurements; one team builds backend and app.

Stage-4 DonHang.App has only web/. Only two browser_web.dart files call the browser: shared/ (local storage for the queue, online event), auth/ (sign-in values across the redirect). The rest of lib/, incl. lib/design/, does not touch it; files needing storage or sign-in go through these two.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0017 @ stage-4 lines 16-21; DonHang.App/lib/shared/browser_web.dart, lib/features/auth/browser_web.dart, imports of lib/shared/browser.dart @ stage-4

claims.text: ADR 0017 options: keep one Flutter code base (add platform folder, rewrite the two browser_web.dart parts); rewrite web with an HTML-building framework plus native apps; native mobile apps keeping Flutter for web. The last two keep design system, Brand, queue in 2-3 places/languages with one team.

The second option's credit: each client fits its platform and web pages can carry HTML for search engines when built on the server; the third option keeps Flutter web because the browser is where the ADR assumes most customers order.

Decision: one Flutter code base for all platforms; for one team the value is one design system, one offline queue, one test suite; shops differ only by Brand on any platform; stage-4 adds no android/ or ios/: no shop needs an installed app enough to pay for store publishing.
A shop's look is a Brand value in lib/design/brand.dart; donHangBrand is the one brand DonHang.App ships.

Consequence 1: the browser downloads Flutter's engine (the part that draws the screens) with main.dart.js (the app's Dart code, Flutter's language, compiled to JavaScript) before drawing the first frame; web-bundle.sh shows that size; it is the decision's first-open cost.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0017 @ stage-4 lines 48-50; Flutter docs: web renderers / initialization

claims.text: The HTML app-web returns for a product holds no product name; Flutter web draws it only after the app runs (what-the-server-sends.sh). Flutter's docs say Flutter web output does not align with what search engines need to index; public product pages: server-built HTML, separate ADR.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0017 @ stage-4 lines 51-55; outputs/stage-4/scripts/frontend/what-the-server-sends.txt; STAGE.md app-web; Flutter web FAQ (search engines)

claims.text: Consequence 3: adding a platform means adding its platform folder and the device API wrapper, not rewriting screens; publishing to the app store is the other cost (PO feedback section).

Reopen conditions: a device feature Flutter cannot reach even through the platform API wrapper; a team per platform, when one code base no longer saves keeping people in sync. On an installed app the platform's wrapper is where a device feature (e.g. a printer) would be reached.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0017 @ stage-4 lines 56-64 ('phần bọc API thiết bị' / 'của nền tảng')

claims.text: A native Android or iOS app does not run inside a browser, so it does not change the first-open cost of customers who order from phone browsers.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: supported deployment platforms (web vs Android/iOS builds)

claims.text: Trade-offs: the chosen option pays in the browser (heavier first open, pages that do not suit search engines); the other two pay in people (same parts kept in step in several languages by one team).

Choices: forty shops wanting Android is not a reopen (add folder, wrapper, store publishing); an unreachable device feature reopens and weighs a native app for that need; a team per platform reopens along team lines.

Cross-platform is cheaper for Đơn Hàng when one team keeps the shared parts; speed must be measured on the devices customers use; liking a framework is not a driver, since every option can draw the screens.
